about: FEMA flood zones the app knows, and the text the dashboard explains them with. key is what the engine stores: FLD_ZONE, except that Zone X is split by ZONE_SUBTY into X_SHADED, X_UNSHADED and X (shading not recorded). risk_rank orders zones when several polygons cover one point, 1 being the highest risk. script/build_flood_zones.py refuses a source with an FLD_ZONE not listed here. Text paraphrases the sources; keep quotes short.

firm_database.title: FEMA: Guidance for the FIRM Database (Nov 2022)

insurance.label: Required
insurance.text: This is a Special Flood Hazard Area, where the mandatory purchase of flood insurance applies: a mortgage from a federally regulated or insured lender, or a federal agency, needs it.

insurance.label: Not required
insurance.text: Outside the Special Flood Hazard Area, federal rules don't require flood insurance. It's still available, and floods happen here too.

insurance.label: Doesn't apply
insurance.text: This isn't a flood zone, so the requirement can't be read from it.

zones.label: Zone VE
zones.summary: Coastal high-hazard area: a 1% or greater chance of flooding each year, with the added danger of storm waves. A detailed study gives base flood elevations.

zones.label: Zone V
zones.summary: Coastal high-hazard area: a 1% or greater chance of flooding each year, with the added danger of storm waves. No base flood elevations are given.

zones.label: Zone AE
zones.summary: High-risk floodplain with a 1% chance of flooding each year. A detailed study gives the base flood elevation: the level the 1% flood is expected to reach. It replaces the older numbered zones A1 to A30.

zones.label: Zone AH
zones.summary: High risk of shallow flooding, usually water ponding, with a 1% chance each year. Base flood elevations are given.

zones.label: Zone AO
zones.summary: High risk of shallow flooding, usually sheet flow on sloping ground, averaging 1 to 3 feet deep, with a 1% or greater chance each year. A flood depth is given instead of an elevation.

zones.label: Zone A
zones.summary: High-risk floodplain with a 1% chance of flooding each year. It was mapped with an approximate study, so no flood depth or base flood elevation is given.

zones.label: Zone AR
zones.summary: Flood risk is temporarily higher while a flood-control system, such as a levee or dam, is built or restored. FEMA says the mandatory purchase requirement applies.

zones.label: Zone A99
zones.summary: A 1% chance of flooding each year, in an area that a federal flood-control system under construction will protect. No depths or base flood elevations are given.

zones.label: Open water
zones.summary: The point is on a mapped body of water, such as a river, lake or the sea. A building here may stand on a pier, or the coordinates may be slightly off.

zones.label: Zone D
zones.summary: Flooding is possible but the hazard hasn't been determined: FEMA has done no flood hazard analysis here. This is not the same as low risk.

zones.label: Zone X (shaded)
zones.summary: Moderate risk: between the reach of the 1% (100-year) and the 0.2% (500-year) floods, also called Zone B. The subtype says when it's something else FEMA shows the same way, such as reduced risk behind a levee, or 1% flooding less than a foot deep.

zones.label: Zone X
zones.summary: Moderate or minimal risk, outside the 1% floodplain. The map doesn't record which: shaded Zone X is moderate, unshaded is minimal.

zones.label: Zone X (unshaded)
zones.summary: Minimal risk: higher than the 0.2% (500-year) flood, also called Zone C. Minimal isn't none.

zones.label: Area not included
zones.summary: FEMA's flood map here shows no flood risk information: the area is mapped on a different map, or isn't mapped by FEMA at all. This is not the same as low risk.

statuses.label: Not on a FEMA flood map
statuses.summary: No FEMA flood zone in this data covers the point. The community may have no digital flood map. This is neither Zone X (minimal risk) nor Zone D (undetermined): there's simply no FEMA information.

statuses.label: Outside the US
statuses.summary: FEMA maps flood zones only in the United States and its territories.

statuses.label: No valid location
statuses.summary: The row's latitude or longitude is missing or invalid, so it couldn't be looked up.

statuses.label: FEMA data not loaded
statuses.summary: This run had no FEMA flood zone data. Build it with script/build_flood_zones.py and run the portfolio again.
